grades.quote: Any level of PTE may be a leaf PTE, so in addition to 4 KiB pages, Sv32 supports 4 MiB _megapages_ . A megapage must be virtually and physically aligned to a 4 MiB boundary; a page-fault exception is raised if the physical address is insufficiently aligned.
grades.reason: This passage covers Sv32, not Sv39. It says any PTE level may be a leaf, and that a megapage must be aligned to its size or a page fault is raised. That is the same concept as Sv39 superpages, but it gives only the Sv32 numbers (4 MiB), so it is auxiliary for an Sv39 question.
This passage describes Sv39 paging with 4 KiB pages, PTE format and address sizes. It says nothing about leaf PTEs at higher levels, superpages or alignment requirements.

grades.quote: If _i_ >0, then this is a superpage translation and _pa.ppn_ [ _i_ -1:0] = _va.vpn_ [ _i_ -1:0].
grades.reason: This passage gives the generic RISC-V translation algorithm. It says a leaf found at level i>0 is a superpage translation, and how the physical address is formed (low PPN bits copied from the VPN). It does not mention Sv39 by name or state the alignment requirement or misaligned-superpage page fault, so it covers only part of the query.
This passage is an Sv48 introduction saying it follows Sv39 and that Sv48 implementations must also support Sv39. It does not discuss leaf PTEs, superpages or alignment.
